# irfanalimd sites

> A personal publishing portal for HTML artifacts (research reports, explainers, learning exercises).
> Hosted on GitHub Pages from the repo `irfanalimd/sites`, branch `main`.
> To publish, upload ONE self-contained HTML file to the repo. No build step, no index to update.

## How to publish

1. Pick a category. Every page must live in exactly one of:
   - `learning` — explainers, tutorials, exercises, things learned or taught
   - `research` — research reports, literature reviews, analyses, findings
   - `random`   — everything else (toys, experiments, one-offs)
   (`til` is also a section, but it's a weekly log edited in place, not a place for standalone pages. See below.)
   If unsure, ask the user; otherwise default to `random`.
2. Pick a short kebab-case slug, e.g. `transformer-attention-explainer`.
3. Write the file to: `p/<category>/<slug>.html` in repo `irfanalimd/sites` on branch `main`.
4. Commit message: `publish: <category>/<slug>`.
5. Tell the user the live URL: `https://sites.irfanali.me/p/<category>/<slug>.html`
   (GitHub Pages takes ~30-60 seconds to update after the commit.)

The homepage (`https://sites.irfanali.me/`) lists every `.html` under `p/<category>/` automatically,
with filters per category. A folder's `index.html` is linked as the folder
(e.g. `p/random/espresso-bench/`), but prefer the flat `p/<category>/<slug>.html` form.

## Rules

- The file must be a complete, self-contained HTML document (`<!doctype html>`, `<title>`, inline CSS/JS).
  External scripts/styles from public CDNs are fine. Do not reference local files that don't exist in the repo.
- Always set a meaningful `<title>` — the homepage uses it as the page name.
- Before writing, check whether `p/<category>/<slug>.html` already exists. If it does, pick a new slug
  unless the user explicitly asked to update that page (updates require the existing file's `sha`).
- Only write inside `p/learning/`, `p/research/`, or `p/random/`. Never modify `index.html`, `llms.txt`, or anything else unless asked.
- Never include secrets, API keys, or private personal data — the site is public.

## Upload methods (use whichever you have)

### GitHub connector / MCP
Use the tool for creating or updating a file (e.g. `create_or_update_file`) with
owner=`irfanalimd`, repo=`sites`, branch=`main`, path=`p/<category>/<slug>.html`, the HTML as content,
and message `publish: <category>/<slug>`.

### gh CLI
    gh api -X PUT repos/irfanalimd/sites/contents/p/<category>/<slug>.html \
      -f message="publish: <category>/<slug>" -f branch=main \
      -f content="$(base64 < page.html | tr -d '\n')"

To update an existing page, first get its sha:
    gh api repos/irfanalimd/sites/contents/p/<category>/<slug>.html --jq .sha
and add `-f sha=<sha>` to the PUT.

### REST API
    PUT https://api.github.com/repos/irfanalimd/sites/contents/p/<category>/<slug>.html
    Authorization: Bearer <token>
    {"message": "publish: <category>/<slug>", "branch": "main", "content": "<base64 of the HTML>"}

### Git (CLI agents)
    git clone https://github.com/irfanalimd/sites && cp page.html sites/p/<category>/<slug>.html
    then commit and push to main.

## TIL (Today I Learned)

If the user asks to add something to "today's learnings" or "TIL", don't create a new page.
Follow the step-by-step instructions in AGENTS.md: https://sites.irfanali.me/AGENTS.md
(In short: append an entry to today's section in `p/til/<this week's Monday>.html`, creating the week from `p/til/_template.html` if needed.)
